newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Meralco seen generating 10 pct sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Meralco seen generating 10 pct sales growth.

text.p: Manila Electric Co (Meralco) is expected to generate profits of close to 4.0 billion pesos for the first nine months of 1996 from 3.34 billion pesos in the same period in 1995, market analysts said on Tuesday.

Analysts said the higher profits will be brought about by Meralco reaching sales volume growth of 10 percent for the first three quarters of the year from last year's 11.90 billion kilowatt-hours (kwh).
Meralco is the Philippines' biggest electricity distributor controlling 75 percent of the market in the northern island of Luzon with a total of 2.8 million customers.
"Among the index heavyweights, Meralco has been one of those performing within expectation," said Helen Alvarez, vice-president for research at Citytrust Investment Bank.
"With increased sales and improved systems loss, the company will likely post 3.8 billion for the first nine months," she said.
She said Meralco may post a 10.6 percent increase in kwh sales for the first nine months as well as for the full year.

"Meralco should be posting a net income of 1.3 billion pesos for the third quarter alone as we see it having the same sales volume growth as it did in the second quarter," said Alex Pomento, analyst at Baring Securities (Phils) Inc.
Meralco posted 2.37 billion pesos in profits for the first half of this year with sales volume rising by 10.6 percent to 8.5 billion kwh.
Alvin Ang of All Asia Capital said the firm will likely realise a 4.3 billion peso nine-month profit level with yearend net income amounting to 5.7 billion peso.
Ang said increased power usage will propel Meralco to post higher full-year profits against last year's 4.4 billion pesos.
Meralco senior vice-president for finance Benito de la Cruz told Reuters on Tuesday the company will probably meet its maximum target of 10 percent growth in electricity sales.
The company had targetted an 8.0 to 10 percent increase in electricity sales volume for the entire year.
"With the growth of over 10 percent for the first eight months, the 10 percent looks like an achievable target for the first nine months," de la Cruz said.
